q: My freight bill shows only the amount, not weight or distance. How do I estimate emissions?
title: Freight bill with no weight or distance
short: First rebuild the missing numbers from other papers for the same shipment: weight from your sales or purchase invoice and packing list, distance from the e-way bill or the two pincodes. Then use tonne-km times a mode factor. Fall back to a spend-based estimate only when that fails, and label it as one.

ul: The goods invoice for the same consignment: quantity in kg or tonnes, or units you can convert with a unit weight.
The packing list or delivery challan: gross weight per carton or pallet.
The lorry receipt (LR or bilty), if the transporter issued one separately from the bill.
Use the gross weight shipped, including packaging, not a charged or minimum weight.
The e-way bill for the consignment, which records an approximate distance in km.
The from and to on the LR or invoice: compute road distance between the two pincodes with a mapping tool and record which one.
For a regular lane, measure it once and reuse the same figure, so your numbers are consistent.

p: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 guidance allows a spend-based method: freight spend x an emission factor per rupee or dollar for transport services. It is quick but rough. Freight rates move with diesel prices, lane and urgency, so the same tonnes can show very different emissions. Remove GST before multiplying, use a factor for the right currency and year, and flag the line as spend-based so you can replace it later.

ol: Ask transporters to print actual weight and distance on every bill or LR.
Keep the e-way bill and the goods invoice with the freight bill.
For regular carriers, ask for fuel used per trip or their own emission figures under ISO 14083 or the GLEC Framework, and state which default values you used where data was missing.

example.title: Worked example: a Mumbai to Delhi shipment
lines: Freight bill: Rs 45,000, no weight or distance
Sales invoice: 400 cartons x 25 kg = 10,000 kg, so 10 t
Distance: about 1,400 km by road between the two pincodes (estimate from a mapping tool)
Factor (illustrative): 0.10 kg CO2e per tonne-km, well-to-wheel
example.note: The 0.10 factor is illustrative. Use a sourced road freight factor for the truck class, from the GLEC Framework or your carrier, and keep the rebuilt weight and distance with their sources.

senseible: Senseible reads freight bills and classifies transport lines as Scope 3, but when weight, distance or mode is missing it marks the line as needing data rather than guessing an emission from the amount. The reader does not turn the amount into emissions on its own; where only the freight cost is known, Senseible can provide a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based and shown with its wider uncertainty.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Technical Guidance for Calculating Scope 3 Emissions (2013), Category 4
